howto.name: Paste a timestamp
howto.text: Enter a Unix epoch (seconds or milliseconds — auto-detected) or an ISO 8601 date string. Click Now to insert the current time.

howto.name: Read all formats side-by-side
howto.text: The tool displays Unix seconds, Unix milliseconds, ISO 8601 (UTC), UTC string, local timezone, and a relative phrase ('in 3 hours', '2 days ago').

howto.name: Copy what you need
howto.text: Click Copy on any row. Useful for filling Cron entries, debugging API timestamps, or formatting logs.

faq.q: How does it know if a number is seconds or milliseconds?
faq.a: By magnitude. Numbers larger than 10^12 (Sep 2001 onward in milliseconds) are treated as milliseconds; smaller as seconds. You can also paste an ISO 8601 string explicitly.

faq.q: Why is the local time different from the UTC time?
faq.a: Your browser's timezone offset is applied. The UTC value is what's actually stored in the timestamp; local is just for human convenience.

faq.q: Can I generate a future timestamp?
faq.a: Yes. Type or paste any past or future ISO date and you'll get the corresponding epoch. The relative phrase will say 'in X days' for the future.
